memory_update.text: POWL is the strongest US-listed underfollowed candidate for the dry-type transformer/power-quality node in this pass, not because it is a transformer pure play, but because its medium-voltage electrical distribution and behind-the-meter data-center backlog directly map to project-gating power infrastructure.
BELFB should be tracked as a second-order component supplier: power solutions, protection, magnetics, and transformer-related data-center components may be hidden inside a generic electronics label.

AMSC is a power-quality/grid-stability hypothesis rather than a transformer-capacity fact pattern; survival into later layers requires evidence of accelerating utility/data-center-linked grid-system orders.

The cleanest dry-type transformer pure play remains Hammond Power Solutions, but it is primarily Canada-listed rather than a standard US-listed equity. US-listed discovery requires adjacent nodes: switchgear, power distribution, magnetics, voltage control, and critical-power systems.

For this node, backlog, lead times, capacity additions, and customer qualification matter more than headline power-demand growth; the key question is whether electrical gear availability can delay facility energization.

node: Dry-type transformers and power-quality electrical equipment
summary: Layer 1B expands the universe around schedule-critical electrical power distribution, conditioning, switchgear, transformers, magnetics, and grid power-quality assets. The strongest underfollowed discovery lane is not the hyperscaler or mega-cap electrical OEM itself, but smaller public suppliers whose order books, component exposure, or customer mix may move earlier than headline data-center or utility capex. This pass includes one mega-cap reference anchor and three underfollowed/speculative names with direct or adjacent exposure to electrical distribution, magnetics, grid power-quality systems, and temporary/critical power infrastructure.
